On 4 February 2017, Messi scored his 27th free-kick for Barcelona in a 3–0 home win over Athletic Bilbao in the league, overtaking Koeman as the club's all-time top-scorer from free-kicks.[[219]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-224) On 23 April, Messi scored twice in a 3–2 away win over Real Madrid. His game-winning goal in stoppage time was his 500th for Barcelona.[[220]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-225) His memorable [celebration](Goal_celebration "Goal celebration") saw him taking off his Barcelona shirt and holding it up to incensed Real Madrid fans – with his name and number facing the crowd.[[221]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-226) On 27 May, Messi scored a goal and set up another for [Paco Alcácer](Paco_Alc%C3%A1cer "Paco Alcácer") in the [2017 Copa del Rey final](2017_Copa_del_Rey_final "2017 Copa del Rey final"), helping Barcelona to a 3–1 victory over [Alavés](Deportivo_Alav%C3%A9s "Deportivo Alavés"), and was named [Man of the Match](Player_of_the_match "Player of the match").[[222]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-227) In total, Messi finished the 2016–17 season with 54 goals, while his 37 goals in La Liga saw him claim both the [Pichichi](Pichichi_Trophy "Pichichi Trophy") and European Golden Boot Awards for the fourth time in his career.[[223]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-228)

#### 2017–18: Domestic double and a record fifth Golden Boot

Messi opened the [2017–18 season](2017%E2%80%9318_FC_Barcelona_season "2017–18 FC Barcelona season") by converting a penalty in Barcelona's 1–3 first leg home defeat to Real Madrid in [Supercopa de España](2017_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2017 Supercopa de España").[[224]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-229) Thereby, Messi also extended his *El Clásico* goalscoring record with the goal being his 24th official and 25th overall.[[225]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-El_ClasicoLM-230) On 9 September, Messi scored his first hat-trick of the 2017–18 league campaign, against Espanyol in *Derbi barceloní*, thus helping to secure a 5–0 home victory for *Blaugrana* over local rivals.[[226]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-231) Messi netted twice against Gianluigi Buffon, on 12 September, as Barça defeated the [last season's Italian champions](2016%E2%80%9317_Serie_A "2016–17 Serie A") Juventus 3–0 at home in the [UEFA Champions League](2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League "2017–18 UEFA Champions League").[[227]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-232) On 19 September, Messi found the net four times in a 6–1 trashing of [Eibar](SD_Eibar "SD Eibar") at the Camp Nou in [La Liga](2017%E2%80%9318_La_Liga "2017–18 La Liga").[[228]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-233) Three weeks later, on 1 October, Messi surpassed his former teammate Carles Puyol to become the third highest appearance maker in the club's history, as he helped Barça defeat Las Palmas 3–0 by assisting [Sergio Busquets](Sergio_Busquets "Sergio Busquets")' opener and later adding two himself in his 594th official game for the club; the league game was played behind closed doors at the Camp Nou due to violence in <Catalonia> relating to an [ongoing independence referendum](2017_Catalan_independence_referendum "2017 Catalan independence referendum").[[229]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-234)

On 18 October, in his 122nd European club appearance, Messi scored his 97th UEFA Champions League goal, and his 100th in all UEFA club competitions, in a 3–1 home victory over [Olympiacos](Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.").[[230]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-235) Messi became only the second player after Cristiano Ronaldo to reach this century milestone, but accomplished it in 21 fewer appearances than the Portuguese counterpart.[[231]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-UEFA100-236) On 4 November, he made his 600th appearance for Barcelona in a 2–1 home win over Sevilla in La Liga.[[232]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-237) Following the reception of his fourth [Golden Boot](European_Golden_Shoe "European Golden Shoe"), Messi signed a new deal with Barcelona on 25 November, keeping him with the club through the [2020–21 season](2020%E2%80%9321_FC_Barcelona_season "2020–21 FC Barcelona season"). His [buyout clause](Buyout_clause "Buyout clause") was set at €700 million.[[233]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-238) On 7 January 2018, Messi made his 400th La Liga appearance with Barcelona in a 3–0 home win over Levante, marking the occasion with his 144th league assist and 365th league goal for the club, the latter of which saw him equal Gerd Müller's record for the most league goals scored for the same club in one of [Europe's top five divisions](Big_Five_(association_football) "Big Five (association football)").[[234]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-Muller-239) A week later, he broke the record, scoring his 366th La Liga goal from a free kick in a 4–2 away win against [Real Sociedad](Real_Sociedad "Real Sociedad").[[234]](Lionel_Messi#cite_note-Muller-239)

**Neymar da Silva Santos Júnior** (born 5 February 1992), known as **Neymar Júnior** or mononymously as **Neymar**, is a Brazilian professional [footballer](Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [forward](Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for [Saudi Pro League](Saudi_Pro_League "Saudi Pro League") club [Al Hilal](Al_Hilal_SFC "Al Hilal SFC") and the [Brazil national team](Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team"). A prolific goalscorer and playmaker, he is widely regarded as one of the best players in the world and one of the best Brazilian players of all time.[[3]](Neymar#cite_note-3)[[4]](Neymar#cite_note-4)[[5]](Neymar#cite_note-5) Neymar has scored at least [100 goals for three different clubs](List_of_world_association_football_records#Goals_and_goalscoring_records "List of world association football records"), making him one of the few players to achieve this feat.[[6]](Neymar#cite_note-6)

Neymar came into prominence at [Santos](Santos_FC "Santos FC"), where he made his professional debut aged 17. Soon becoming the Brazilian's league star player, he won the [2011 Copa Libertadores](2011_Copa_Libertadores "2011 Copa Libertadores") with Santos, being their first since 1963. He was named the [South American Footballer of the Year](South_American_Footballer_of_the_Year "South American Footballer of the Year") in [2011](2011_South_American_Footballer_of_the_Year "2011 South American Footballer of the Year") and [2012](2012_South_American_Footballer_of_the_Year "2012 South American Footballer of the Year"), and relocated to Europe to join [Barcelona](FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") in 2013. In his second season, as part of Barcelona's attacking trio with [Lionel Messi](Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") and [Luis Suárez](Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez"), dubbed *MSN*, he won the [continental treble](Treble_(association_football) "Treble (association football)") of [La Liga](La_Liga "La Liga"), the [Copa del Rey](Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey"), and the [UEFA Champions League](UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). Motivated to be the focal player at club level, Neymar unexpectedly transferred to [Paris Saint-Germain](Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C.") (PSG) in 2017[[7]](Neymar#cite_note-7) for €222 million, which made him [the most expensive player ever](List_of_most_expensive_association_football_transfers "List of most expensive association football transfers").[[note 1]](Neymar#cite_note-10) Despite recurring injuries and consequential limited game time in Paris, he was voted [Ligue 1 Player of the Year](Ligue_1_Player_of_the_Year "Ligue 1 Player of the Year") in his debut season, helped PSG attain an historic domestic [quadruple](List_of_association_football_teams_to_have_won_four_or_more_trophies_in_one_season "List of association football teams to have won four or more trophies in one season") and reach its first ever [Champions League final](2020_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2020 UEFA Champions League final") in the [2019–20 season](2019%E2%80%9320_Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C._season "2019–20 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season"), and established himself as the highest scoring Brazilian player in Champions League history.[[10]](Neymar#cite_note-11)

Debuting for Brazil aged 18, Neymar is the [all-time top goalscorer](Brazil_national_football_team#Top_goalscorers "Brazil national football team") for his national team with 79 goals in 126 matches. He won the [2013 FIFA Confederations Cup](2013_FIFA_Confederations_Cup "2013 FIFA Confederations Cup"), winning the [Golden Ball](Golden_Ball_(FIFA_Confederations_Cup) "Golden Ball (FIFA Confederations Cup)"). His participation in the [2014 FIFA World Cup](2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") and [2015 Copa América](2015_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2015 Copa América") was cut short by injury and a suspension, respectively, before captaining Brazil to their first [Olympic gold medal](Olympic_gold_medal "Olympic gold medal") in [men's football](Football_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament") at the [2016 Summer Olympics](2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"), having already achieving a [silver medal](Olympic_silver_medal "Olympic silver medal") at the [2012](2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") edition. Having renounced the captaincy, he featured at the [2018 World Cup](2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup"), and after missing the [2019 Copa América](2019_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2019 Copa América") through injury, helped Brazil to a runner-up finish at the [2021 tournament](2021_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2021 Copa América").

Neymar finished third for the [FIFA Ballon d'Or](FIFA_Ballon_d'Or "FIFA Ballon d'Or") in [2015](2015_FIFA_Ballon_d'Or "2015 FIFA Ballon d'Or") and [2017](2017_Ballon_d'Or "2017 Ballon d'Or"), has been awarded the [FIFA Puskás Award](FIFA_Pusk%C3%A1s_Award "FIFA Puskás Award"), has been named in the [FIFA FIFPro World11](FIFPro "FIFPro") twice, and the [UEFA Champions League Squad of the Season](UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") three times. Off the pitch, he ranks among the world's most prominent sportsmen. *<SportsPro>* named him the most marketable athlete in the world in 2012 and 2013, and <ESPN> cited him as the world's fourth-most-famous athlete in 2016. In 2017, *[Time](Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* included him in its annual list of the [100 most influential people in the world](Time_100 "Time 100").[[11]](Neymar#cite_note-:0-12) In 2018, *[France Football](France_Football "France Football")* ranked Neymar the world's third-highest-paid footballer. The following year, *<Forbes>* ranked him the [world's third-highest-paid athlete](Forbes'_list_of_the_world's_highest-paid_athletes "Forbes' list of the world's highest-paid athletes"),[[12]](Neymar#cite_note-Forbes-13) dropping a spot to fourth in 2020.[[13]](Neymar#cite_note-14)

The **2015 UEFA Champions League final** was the final match of the [2014–15 UEFA Champions League](2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League "2014–15 UEFA Champions League"), the 60th season of Europe's premier club [football](Association_football "Association football") tournament organised by <UEFA>, and the 23rd season since it was renamed from the European Champion Clubs' Cup to the [UEFA Champions League](UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). It was played at the [Olympiastadion](Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") in <Berlin>, Germany, on 6 June 2015, between Italian side [Juventus](Juventus_F.C. "Juventus F.C.") and Spanish side [Barcelona](FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").

For the second time – after [2010](2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final") – both teams came into the final with the possibility of definitively winning a [continental treble](Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)"), having each won their national league and cup for the season. Barcelona scored the only goal of the first half after four minutes, through [Ivan Rakitić](Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić"). Ten minutes after the interval, Juventus equalised with a goal by [Álvaro Morata](%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata"). In the 68th minute, [Luis Suárez](Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez") put Barcelona back in the lead, and Barcelona's win was confirmed when <Neymar> scored with the last kick of the game. It was Barcelona's fifth trophy in the competition, and sealed their second treble, the other coming in [2009](2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final"). It was also Juventus' sixth defeat in a European Cup final, the most by any club, a record they previously shared with [Bayern Munich](FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") and [Benfica](S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica").

As winners, Barcelona earned the right to play against the winners of the [2014–15 UEFA Europa League](2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Europa_League "2014–15 UEFA Europa League"), [Sevilla](Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"), in the [2015 UEFA Super Cup](2015_UEFA_Super_Cup "2015 UEFA Super Cup"), and won that match 5–4. They also qualified to enter the [2015 FIFA Club World Cup](2015_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2015 FIFA Club World Cup") in Japan as the UEFA representative, going on to beat Argentina's [River Plate](CA_River_Plate "CA River Plate") in the [final](2015_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final "2015 FIFA Club World Cup final").

## Venue

The [Olympiastadion](Olympiastadion_(Berlin) "Olympiastadion (Berlin)") was announced as the venue for the final at the UEFA Executive Committee meeting in London on 23 May 2013.[[4]](2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-4) This was the first European Cup/Champions League final hosted in Berlin.[[5]](2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-5)

The current Olympiastadion was built for the [1936 Summer Olympics](1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics") in the western part of the city.[[6]](2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-6) Since 1985, the stadium has hosted the finals of both the <DFB-Pokal> and its [female equivalent](DFB-Pokal_(women) "DFB-Pokal (women)"). The Olympiastadion hosts the [Internationales Stadionfest](ISTAF_Berlin "ISTAF Berlin"), which was an [IAAF Golden League](IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") event from 1998 to 2009. The stadium hosted the [2009 World Championships in Athletics](2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics").[[7]](2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final#cite_note-Host1-7)

Hazard began his senior career with [Ligue 1](Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club [Lille](Lille_OSC "Lille OSC") in 2007 at the age of 16 and soon became an integral part of the Lille team under manager [Rudi Garcia](Rudi_Garcia "Rudi Garcia"). In his first full season, he became the first non-French player to win the [Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year](Ligue_1_Young_Player_of_the_Year "Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year") award, and the following season became the first player to win the award twice. In the [2010–11 season](2010%E2%80%9311_in_French_football "2010–11 in French football"), he won the [league and cup double](Double_(association_football) "Double (association football)") and, as a result of his performances, was named the [Ligue 1 Player of the Year](Ligue_1_Player_of_the_Year "Ligue 1 Player of the Year"), the youngest player to win the award.

After making over 190 appearances and scoring 50 goals for Lille, Hazard signed for English club [Chelsea](Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") in June 2012. He won the [UEFA Europa League](UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") in his first season and the [PFA Young Player of the Year](PFA_Young_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Young Player of the Year") in his second. Two years later he won his second English league title as Chelsea won the [2016–17](2016%E2%80%9317_Premier_League "2016–17 Premier League") Premier League. **Gareth Frank Bale** [MBE](Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (born 16 July 1989) is a Welsh former professional [footballer](Association_football "Association football") who played as a [winger](Winger_(association_football) "Winger (association football)"), most notably for [Tottenham Hotspur](Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") and [Real Madrid](Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"). He is widely regarded as one of the best footballers of his generation and one of the greatest Welsh players of all time.[[2]](Gareth_Bale#cite_note-BestLeftWingerNeville-2)[[3]](Gareth_Bale#cite_note-3)[[4]](Gareth_Bale#cite_note-4)[[5]](Gareth_Bale#cite_note-auto1-5) He was best known for his explosive pace, athleticism, and powerful strikes from distance.

Bale began his professional career at [Southampton](Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C."), playing at [left-back](Defender_(association_football)#Full-back "Defender (association football)") before moving to Tottenham in 2007. From the 2009–10 season, under the guidance of [Harry Redknapp](Harry_Redknapp "Harry Redknapp"), Bale became an integral part of the team and transformed into a winger. He went on to receive several individual honours, including two [PFA Players' Player of the Year](PFA_Players'_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Players' Player of the Year") awards and three [PFA Team of the Year](PFA_Team_of_the_Year "PFA Team of the Year") inclusions. In September 2013, Real Madrid signed Bale for a then [world-record transfer fee](List_of_most_expensive_association_football_transfers "List of most expensive association football transfers") of £85.1 million (€100.8 million). Being part of the subsequent trio dubbed *BBC*, alongside [Cristiano Ronaldo](Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") and [Karim Benzema](Karim_Benzema "Karim Benzema"), Bale helped the club to win the [Copa del Rey](2013%E2%80%9314_Copa_del_Rey "2013–14 Copa del Rey") and the [Champions League](2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League"), scoring in both finals.

Although Bale experienced a decrease in game time from 2015 onwards due to continual injuries, he was amongst the top three nominees for the [2015-16 UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award](UEFA_Men's_Player_of_the_Year_Award#2015–16 "UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award"), scored an [overhead kick](Overhead_kick "Overhead kick") in Real Madrid's [2018 UEFA Champions League Final](2018_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2018 UEFA Champions League Final") victory, and was awarded the [FIFA Club World Cup Golden Ball](FIFA_Club_World_Cup_Golden_Ball "FIFA Club World Cup Golden Ball") in [2018](2018_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2018 FIFA Club World Cup"). In [2020–21](2020%E2%80%9321_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2020–21 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season"), he returned to Tottenham on [loan](Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)"), before playing his final season in Madrid. In his nine-year tenure, Bale won 15 trophies, including three [La Liga](La_Liga "La Liga") titles and five Champions Leagues. He joined [MLS](Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") club [Los Angeles FC](Los_Angeles_FC "Los Angeles FC") in July 2022 before retiring in January 2023, aged 33.

Bale made his senior international debut for [Wales](Wales_national_football_team "Wales national football team") in May 2006, becoming the youngest player at that point to represent the nation. He then went on to earn 111 caps and scored 41 international goals, making him Wales' [most capped player](Wales_national_football_team#Most_caps "Wales national football team") and [top goalscorer of all time](Wales_national_football_team#Most_goals "Wales national football team"). He was the top scorer for Wales in their successful qualifying campaign for [UEFA Euro 2016](UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016"), scoring seven times; he subsequently represented Wales in the final tournament as they reached the semi-finals, scoring three goals. He later featured for the side at [Euro 2020](UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020") and was pivotal in Wales' qualifying for the [2022 FIFA World Cup](2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), ending a 64-year appearance drought at the [World Cup](FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"). He was named [Welsh Footballer of the Year](Welsh_Footballer_of_the_Year "Welsh Footballer of the Year") a record six times.
